title: Characterisation of soil micro-topography using a depth camera
author: Grundy, Ghimire, et al.

steps.title: Assemble camera mounting frame
steps.instruction: Build an aluminium frame with adjustable legs, attach a tripod mount, and suspend the Intel RealSense D415 depth camera from it.

steps.title: Level camera and target
steps.instruction: Place the target (e.g., 400 mm × 400 mm plywood) on the frame, then use a spirit level to make the camera and the target surface horizontal.

steps.title: Connect camera to computer
steps.instruction: Attach the camera to a computer with a USB 3.1 cable and install the Intel RealSense Viewer or the Python SDK wrapper for image acquisition.

steps.title: Calibrate camera if needed
steps.instruction: Follow the factory‑supplied calibration instructions to recalibrate the camera; otherwise use the pre‑calibrated state.

steps.title: Configure automated image capture
steps.instruction: Write/run a Python script that (a) initializes the sensor, (b) waits for five frames to allow exposure adjustment, (c) captures a single frame at a user‑set interval, (d) disables the sensor, and (e) clears the frame buffer; the camera operates at 30 fps.

steps.title: Conduct accuracy height series
steps.instruction: Set the camera at each of six heights—1500 mm, 1350 mm, 1200 mm, 1055 mm, 900 mm, and 750 mm—above the centred 400 mm × 400 mm plywood, level the setup, capture an image, and record the average distance of points within the target region; compare each average to a tape‑measure reading (±0.05 mm).

steps.title: Measure precision at 1055 mm
steps.instruction: Position the camera at 1055 mm height, capture 49 consecutive frames using the script, and calculate the variation; 95 % of the repeats should lie within ±1 mm of the mean.

steps.title: Evaluate surface‑area estimation
steps.instruction: Build six artificial models by placing 0 to 6 plastic hemispheres (60 mm diameter) on the plywood, acquire images at the same six heights, compute the measured surface area for each model, and fit a linear regression against the theoretical surface area.

steps.title: Assess soil micro‑topography repeatability
steps.instruction: Remove vegetation from two soil patches (intact and damaged), set the camera at ~1000 mm height to capture a 1200 mm × 800 mm area, acquire 20 repetitions per surface, then calculate for each surface the mean elevation, its standard deviation, and the random roughness defined as the standard deviation of slope‑corrected elevation measurements.

steps.title: Post‑process point clouds (optional)
steps.instruction: Apply desired SDK filters (spatial, decimation, disparity transform, temporal, hole‑filling) while noting that decimation and temporal filters reduce point count, whereas spatial, disparity, and hole‑filling may smooth genuine roughness; choose filters based on the trade‑off between noise reduction and preservation of micro‑topography.
